answer: Reputation-weighted resource pricing: each agent's call quota and priority derive from a slowly-updated trust score, computed like a prism splitting observed behavior into consistency bands. An operator's credibility is tracked in an atlas mapping accounts to shared infrastructure fingerprints, so cloned agents inherit the lowest score among linked accounts. A raven quietly flags accounts whose behavior correlates too tightly with known clones. Cloning therefore yields quotas as low as the worst linked identity, while honest sustained behavior raises quota cheaply.
